_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, margin, expense and receivables signals with Google's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Alphabet is a collection of businesses -- the largest of which, of course, is Google.' 'We generate revenues primarily by delivering online advertising that consumers find relevant and that advertisers find cost-effective.' 'We generate a significant portion of our revenues from advertising, and reduced spending by advertisers or a loss of partners could seriously harm our business.' 'We face intense competition.' 'As our growth rate has slowed, the cyclicality and seasonality in our business has become more pronounced and caused our operating results to fluctuate.' 'In addition, expenditures by advertisers tend to be cyclical, reflecting overall economic conditions and budgeting and buying patterns.' (FY2015 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; no theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a search and advertising company on these dates (OFFSHORE is scoped to IT services; CLOUD, live from 2012-10-30, is scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and this 10-K names the cloud only as Google's own products ('Google includes our main internet products such as Search, Ads, Commerce, Maps, YouTube, Apps, Cloud, Android, Chrome, Google Play'), so it is out of scope (the AVGO FY2012 and NVDA reading); ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (from 2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (from 2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels), so the watch list is empty; the competition named is a competitive field, not a theme, and stays here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (worst year FY06-FY15, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +20.1%/yr (Q2 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +20.1%/yr (FY06-FY15 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +40.6%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY15, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: GOOG (retrospective, 2016-08-19) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.19x (44.1% downside to Bear $433.25 / +37.1% upside to Bull $1062.92) | Adj composite 1.70 vs market 2.57: gap -0.87 [OVERVALUED] | +68% above the EPP floor $462.46 (19x FY16E $24.34) | Conservative 2-yr case: +0.6% total (+0.3%/yr) | At 31.9x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $1,025.49 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +21.3% YoY in Q2 2016, forward revenues +21.3% (Q2 2016 revenue growth (no Q3 2016 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
